title: 01 · Research the example-game database, real previews, categories and source links
body:
## Problem and outcome

The supplied seed records are research leads, not a reviewed catalog. Create the first useful evidence-backed database of example games and reusable systems so product decisions and the first UI use real projects, real images, and honest source/rights information.

## Priority and dependencies

- Sequence: 01; priority: P0; phase: Research foundation.
- Depends on: None; ready to start.
- Before dependent implementation, document independent reviewer evidence that the prerequisite behavior, interfaces and data needed by this issue pass. An unrelated pending visual criterion need not block that work; unresolved required behavior or interfaces still block it. Independent work may proceed in parallel; this does not close a partially accepted prerequisite issue. This issue is not authorization to execute the entire backlog.

## Scope and boundaries

Research before building app infrastructure. Deliver provisional structured JSON plus a readable CSV/Markdown view, a data dictionary, image manifest and gap report under `research/catalog/`; later issues migrate these into production contracts. Start with the six supplied seeds, then expand across racing, platforming, RPG/action, exploration/geospatial, simulation/management/tycoon, builders and RTS. Include OpenRCT2, OpenTTD, 3d.city, SlimCity and Fable Cities as leads requiring re-verification. Favor Three.js/R3F for near-term integration while recording Phaser/Godot/Unity and native-only projects with explicit discovery-only limits. Do not execute arbitrary upstream builds on the host, manufacture screenshots, or claim source visibility grants reuse rights.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Research at least 30 distinct repositories or independently useful subprojects; deduplicate by provider identity and subproject path, and maintain a coverage table by genre, runtime and content kind.
- [ ] Target 20 eligible examples for internal discovery only when evidence supports eligibility. If fewer clear the bar, deliver all reviewed candidates with an explicit shortfall, rejection reasons, coverage gaps and concrete follow-up leads; do not lower evidence standards to meet a count.
- [ ] Every row includes canonical project/repository URLs, upstream provider ID when available, subproject path, title, creator, description, pinned full commit or explicit unresolved revision, research date/reviewer and primary evidence links.
- [ ] Record browser demo URL and dated reachability separately from interactive play evidence, source/demo relationship, controls and platform support. Identify native-only, broken, blocked, removed and unknown cases without a playable-now claim.
- [ ] Separate content kind, genres/intents, source-backed capabilities, dimension, perspective/camera, visual style, runtime/version, physics/rendering stack, controls/platform, assets/authoring tools and reuse conditions. Include simulation clocks, pause/speed, construction, zoning, economy, workers, resource loops, pathfinding and production queues only where source or clearly labeled observations support each tag.
- [ ] For each candidate, record actual upstream screenshot/media evidence or a justified missing-preview status. Each displayable image has original source/capture URL, image-to-game identity, capture date, creator/credit, permission/license evidence, allowed use, dimensions, digest and descriptive alt text; store a derivative only when its display/redistribution rights are resolved. Do not hotlink or substitute generated artwork to bypass unresolved image rights.
- [ ] Deliver a minimum useful set of authentic, rights-cleared display previews for at least 10 distinct researched examples spanning at least four genre/intent categories, with a reviewable contact sheet linked to their image manifests. Individual missing-preview statuses are allowed, but inability to clear this minimum leaves image acceptance pending with a documented blocker; illustrative or generated substitutes cannot satisfy it.
- [ ] Resolve project code, selected-file, asset and dataset rights separately with exact evidence and obligations; missing or contradictory rights stay in the research queue and block corresponding reuse/export. Screenshot display permission is distinct from code licensing.
- [ ] Provide a curated shortlist explaining why each example is useful, candidate source paths for useful systems, known coupling and unknowns. All capability labels distinguish proposed, observed and statically inspected claims; no entry claims an integration test.
- [ ] Include a repeatable link/data audit command or documented workflow, a per-field completeness report and estimated source-review effort from the first ten reviews.

## Validation evidence

Run structure/duplicate/link checks. Independently spot-check the whole 30-record inventory and review every record proposed as eligible, with a contact sheet of rights-cleared previews and primary-source citations. Record real browser/device checks for playable claims and missing evidence explicitly. A second researcher must be able to trace any screenshot, category and source claim to its evidence.

## Required coder and critical reviewer loop

Follow the [development workflow](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/main/docs/development-workflow.md) and the issue-specific evidence below.

1. Assign a coder subagent to implement this issue with production-grade error handling, clear interfaces, and focused changes. For research, the author subagent produces the research dataset and evidence instead of unnecessary application code.
2. Assign a separate critical reviewer subagent who did not author the changes. Give the reviewer the issue, exact revision/diff, acceptance checklist, and evidence. The reviewer independently inspects the output and runs relevant checks; author self-review does not satisfy this gate.
3. The reviewer checks primary-source citations, pinned revisions, capability/category claims, actual image identity and display rights, representative demo observations, and every proposed eligible record; unsupported claims remain unresolved.
4. For any UI introduced or changed during this issue, attach desktop and mobile screenshots with viewport/browser, scenario and revision; the reviewer must inspect them and critique visual design, accessibility and interaction states under the [design-direction policy](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/main/docs/design-direction.md). Any styling remains provisional until the user selects a mockup baseline; record pending final visual acceptance explicitly. Otherwise explicitly record screenshots as not applicable and review the relevant data, CLI, protocol or runtime evidence.
5. The coder fixes each blocking finding and reruns affected checks; the same independent reviewer re-reviews the new revision and evidence. Repeat until the reviewer explicitly records PASS with no unresolved blocking acceptance or design findings. Do not weaken criteria merely to obtain approval.
6. Save commands, actual results, evidence paths, reviewer findings, fix references and final verdict in `docs/reviews/catalog-research/`. A blocked external dependency or unavailable test remains open with its limitation; it is never a simulated success. Close only after the independent PASS.

## Source requirements

- `HeadStart-Starter-Package/Playparts-Technical-PRD-v0.3.md` — Initial catalog target; Search ontology and taxonomy; Seed catalog and evidence notes; Licensing attribution and provenance; Review queue and health.
- `HeadStart-Starter-Package/Product-Direction-v0.4.md` — Product promise; Product surfaces; What the system should have opinions about.
- `AGENTS.md` — source truth, trust boundaries, UI evidence and working guidance.
